reviews.text: Sian Heder delivers an emotional film that plays all the right notes to move the audience, much like a puppeteer controlling its marionette.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: CODA has all the hallmarks of a Sundance darling. ... The thing is, it’s a formula that works, here yielding an entertaining, moving story that illuminates a community underrepresented onscreen.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Though the film's conflict is nicely wrapped up by the end with predictability and little realistic effort, it doesn't take away from the heartwarming content, often humorous tone, and feel-good nature.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: It leaves you in a puddle of emotion, but by the end you realize it’s a good puddle. It’s a puddle of satisfaction, hope, and a full heart.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: Coda refuses to rehash the well-worn tropes of this May-December subgenre, swapping it out for an almost Bergman-like contemplativeness.
reviews.author: Aditya Mani Jha

reviews.text: CODA is a delight, a warm hug of a film that knows its genre and makes the very most of it. Siân Heder’s script is simple, and the message that she sends is heartfelt. A crowd-pleaser with love to spare.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: ...weakening a film whose representation of the underrepresented is so intense at times that its dependence on Hallmark-like characteristics is more than mildly disappointing.
reviews.author: Mo Muzammal

reviews.text: A Must Watch Winner that will delight you
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Siân Heder offers her impeccable direction and beautifully written screenplay, which is packed with emotionally powerful moments that left me tearing up for the last forty-five minutes.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: CODA is a simple, moving film with great performances.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: What so impressed me and makes this a movie I'd recommend is how writer and director Sian Heder used sound -- and the lack of sound -- to showcase the beauty and emotional power of music to connect with people.
reviews.author: Connie Guglielmo

reviews.text: With one of the most clever scripts of the year, CODA made me feel a lot of feelings.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: "CODA is sweet, sincere and genuinely funny in parts, and it’s precisely the kind of coming-of-age film that we should hope to see more of. "
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: ...alternates between being contrived and genuinely moving.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: CODA is cathartic. A film that put a giant lump in your throat while at the same time lifting your spirits.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: It’s a movie about a cute kid who wants to go off to Fancy School in the City. The deafness is very much incidental.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The humor makes for a great compliment to the coming-of-age drama which follows a pretty conventional blueprint but enhances it with a uniquely fresh perspective.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Films like these highlight the differences and similarities and seek the bridge that gap as well as share a story of struggle, growth, and exploration. This film does all three magnificently and will bring audiences to tears.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: ... The bones of The Belier Family are fleshed out in new, muscular ways by writer-director Sian Heder, working with deaf creative collaborators Anne Tomasetti and Alexandria Wailes.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: CODA works well to deliver effective drama, music and some comedy with character conflicts that are relatable.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: A foreseeable story that's adamant to be kind and only threat is sweetening the characters and the situations they go through, and makes it clear that the ending, too, will be conveniently happy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text:
What hurts the most is the almost algorithmic…mechanisms of tabletop drama.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: A feel good triumph and standard coming of age narrative. The opportunities afforded the deaf cast are cause for celebration, even if their stories would have been more exciting to see compared to the familiar YA romance of the hearing protagonist
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: CODA is a classic story of intergenerational conflict spiced up with a culture clash narrative between the deaf and hearing communities. The execution is nearly flawless
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Heart sometimes beats prestige and we couldn't be more OK with that.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Funny and poignant by turns, CODA is solid entertainment.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: CODA isn't the best film of the year, but it's the heartfelt uplifting story we all need.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Much about her experiences are left unsaid and undeveloped. In spite of this, does it make for entertaining viewing? Yes, for most of its running time, but had it not won Best Picture, you would likely never think of it as a movie of the year.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: It’s a charming movie, and recommended, but only if you’re ready for something that plays like an elevated movie-of-the-week that feels designed for the small screen.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: Coda is a Mort (‘Middle Of Road Tearjerker’) and if that’s what you like, you will like this.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: This well-intentioned, feel-good drama about a child of deaf adults negotiating the trials of adolescence is a pretty rote affair...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Out of all the films nominated for the 2022 Academy Awards, Coda is one of the best examples of the power of storytelling.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: This film boasts laughs and love and tears. Its one Im glad to give loud cheers!
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: The story is completely predictable, with the pleasures of the film to be found in the development of the characters and the feeling that we are learning about a world-within-a-world, namely that of the deaf.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Presented with a group of teens singing David Bowie’s “Starman,” I would watch in silent frustration, too. The issue is that for me it would be easier to forget.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: ...an erratic yet mostly rewarding drama...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: There's no shame in a formula done well, and CODA does more than well.
reviews.author: Belen Edwards

reviews.text: I love this movie, I really do. I had underestimated its potential. It's a big warm fuzzy hug of a movie - everyone should check it out.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Uniquely beautiful to watch.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: This charming coming-of-age story will most likely leave you in tears. While on the surface, it touches upon the usual topics of graduation, crushes, and social anxiety within a high school setting, the film is so much more than that.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: What sets CODA apart from other family dramas is, this was never intended to be Ruby Rossis solo journey. Heder takes time building out the world around the Rossi family, crafting a coming-of-age tale focused on a family forced to grow up
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: It brilliantly balances the kinds of cinematic themes and components that play so well  humor, innocence, precise scripting, powerful performances, stirring music, and a convincing tenderness - even if its formula is apparent.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: CODA is a refreshing film for its marked humanity ... Its unique focus and concerns lift the work above the danger of becoming formulaic.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: A narrative and conceptual tangled mess, much more worried about moving and making the crowd cry at all costs than shaping a truthful and organic story with a minimum number of surprises to break its disappointing routine.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: It has a well-intentioned touch when it embraces the setbacks of a deaf family, but at times I have the feeling that its dramatic comedy is sinking in the sea of predictable coming-of-age formulas. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The sense of calculation makes the journey feel like a lockstep march; the movie’s sense of a story that’s dictated rather than observed makes its good feelings feel bad.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: As a story of maturity, CODA is excellent and as an example of inclusiveness it is pivotal.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: CODA is admirably made but conventional storytelling.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text:
This tearjerker rolls deep.
Emilia Jones gives a fierce performance.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: A tender celebration of the resilience of a family unit and the beauty of mutually sacrificial, self-giving love.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: "CODA" is an exquisite, powerhouse of a movie. Hold on to your heart, because the irresistible "CODA" will steal it!
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: Emilia Jones is a real revelation in this movie. She gives a beautiful performance and has a lovely singing voice. Eugenio Derbez gives a wonderful performance as the smart, wise-cracking school music teacher.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: CODA is a brilliantly humane, uplifting film full of fine performances-and it's a leap forward for the representation of people with disabilities on film.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: This jaded heart has been jolted. CODA is the Best Film of 2021.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: No theatrics, no gimmicks - just a wonderful coming-of-age gem that aims directly at the heart and hits the bullseye.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: The beautiful use of American Sign Language throughout will make you want to learn it.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Though we'd love to see a Deaf story that doesn't need to use a Hearing protagonist as an "entry point," the unique and under-seen family dynamic portrayed on screen still feels fresh.
reviews.author: Aditya Joshi

reviews.text: Apple TV+'s enlightening movie offers interesting insights.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: ...this is a delicate, wholesome movie that doesn't hold back on the big finale...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Sian Heder is a real find. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: A film that moves along well-known paths in a way that surprises and excites. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: What really works about this film are the rougher edges, the moments of ambivalence on the margins (and even at the centre) and its firm awareness of uncertainty.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: A love letter to family
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: With warmth, humor and a strong cast, CODA has turned a conventional family dynamic and an oft-told tale of a teenager pursuing her dream into something special.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: The naturalness and honesty of the dialogues... is what makes CODA an enjoyable film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: CODA's story is quite powerful... The rest of the plot about self-improvement and fighting for the right thing can be trite, but it works, and it works very well. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Whether a remake had been absolutely necessary for this is a matter of opinion. But on its own, CODA is a nice crowd-pleaser. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Not bad, the actors are very convincing but, I insist, is there no way for the gringos to read subtitles and watch the original films? In this case, La famille Bélier, was a much better movie.
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Heder takes the movie in various directions with its mix of coming-of-age drama, high school angst, broad comedy, and working-class themes, but it all works, coming together as a memorable family movie night pick for parents with teens.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Lamentably, only the humorous moments prevail.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: What I loved about Sian Heder's film, the title of which stands for Child of Deaf Adults, is that it created magic without much effort or showing off.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Predictable, yes, but no reasonable person wants failure for this genuinely warm and loving family.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Heder cuts to silence during Ruby's solo at the school choir concert in order to give us the family's perspective, and the effect is as profound as it is heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Films like CODA represent a changing of the Hollywood guard - more folks at the table, putting people in the jobs they should've had all along.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Try not to be moved by this loving, needy, overwhelmed and surprisingly horny family confronting change.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: Bravo to co-writer and sole director Sian Heder for breathing fresh life into an old but reliable storyline.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: If there's a flaw to "CODA" - the title stems from the term "child of deaf adult" -- it may be that it wears its brimming heart on its sleeve to such an extent that it occasionally nears that fine line into formula.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: Bring tissues. You may sail away on an ocean of tears.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: [Emilia Jones] captures Ruby's love for music and for her family, even when the burden of being its only hearing member grows wearying.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Whilst Coda is enjoyably understated and thoroughly enchanting it doesn't mean it is in no way formulaic and it raises the question of whether certain tangents in the story had been fully rounded out.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: Filled with endearing, empathetic performances, CODA tells a fairly conventional coming-of-age story that is no less charming for being familiar.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: Yes, a lot of it is very corny. But it works- and in the age of Ted Lasso, I feel like it's going to truly hit the Apple TV+ audience specifically.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The possibilities for saccharine uplift are legion -- yet Heder and her cast sidestep all the pitfalls by giving us characters that are fully formed and absolutely believable.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Emotionally satisfying and funny to boot, CODA is an absolute delight.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: [H]eartwarming and funny ... [CODA] also is about how children yearn to be independent and find their voice. ... There are many ways to communicate, CODA reminds us. Many languages of love.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: A coming-of-age story meant to move. And while the beats of the film may be predictable, it's no less affecting.
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: CODA at its core is a simple coming-of-age story but executed as flawlessly as you can expect, whilst also putting a much-needed spotlight on the deaf community.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: CODA isn't reinventing the wheel, but it's a solid feel-good film that you can't help but fall in love with.
reviews.author: Jean Henegan

reviews.text: Coda is perfection from start to finish, keeping audiences engaged through humor, heart, and genuine craftsmanship.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: CODA's characters are so appealing in their feisty quirkiness and family warmth, that it is the kind of film you will want to revisit. The story is both universal and unique to these characters, and that is a combination that is hard to beat.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Ruby is an underdog worth rooting for, and Jones is terrific. She's like a cross between the young Winona Ryder and the young Kate Winslet. The comparison flatters all three.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: You'll laugh, cry and all steps in between at this vital family entertainment with a title that stands for Children of Deaf Adults. Oscar winner Marlee Matlin and newcomer Emilia Jones turn this emotional powerhouse into one of the year's best.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: "CODA" is one of the best coming of age stories to come down the pike in a long time and it showcases Emilia Jones with her fine and assured performance.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Heartwarming coming-of-age story that illustrates how singing can set you free.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The Hallmark Channel called and they want their movie back... but anyone with a pulse will find this moving.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: CODA is a tender family drama that finds a fresh approach to the familiar tale of what is lost and what is gained by breaking away to find one's own voice.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: This is one of the most heartfelt, exuberantly humane movies in recent memory.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Charming crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: CODA hasn't reinvented the wheel, but it's a satisfying watch with some truly beautifully rendered sequences.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Heder, who spent time on the Massachusetts coast when growing up, knows exactly how a narrative can be enriched by the colours, moods and customs of its setting. You get to know the Rossis very well, and they're great company.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Each performance breathes life and nuance into what could easily have been a misfire. Instead, the result is tremendously sweet, uproariously funny and one of the best crowd-pleasers this year.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Patronizing, condescending, and that's not even the worst of it.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: CODA has all the makings of a crowd-pleaser and it hits those strides with heart and soul.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: It lives up to its title, all right, with an ending that takes all the the little details, moments, memories and needle drops from the first two acts, and brings them back for a rousing, uplifting, wipe-the-tears-from-your-face encore.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: A magical little movie with a giant heart.
reviews.author: Jade Budowski

reviews.text: The film is a meticulously, perhaps even cynically crafted crowd-pleaser. Even those alive to its tactics might find themselves wiping away a tear or two.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Nearly undone by schmaltz and cliche at every corner, but it transcends its weepy tone through sheer force of will and the unique charm of presenting a deaf family without the self-defeating need to make them a monolithic model minority franchise.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: 'CODA' is a movie overflowing with heart and love. And Heder doesn't pander by using the family's deafness as a tool for pity or understanding.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Director Heder avoids sugarcoating the trials and tribulations of life, and she has a cast, especially the four principals, that delivers the goods in every frame.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: I was won over by the strength of the performances and the moments of genuine, heartfelt emotion.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Heartwarming and life-affirming, while making space for more authentic stories in the future of both indie and studio productions, CODA is one of the most joyful films of 2021.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: "...a layered, rich movie experience that will sweep you off your feet."
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: A fabulous feel-good coming-of-age story that will steal your heart. One of the most satisfying films of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The first scene only hints at where this small, special movie takes us, particularly with an uncanny ability to surprise as much with plot motivations as it does to inspire either a silent teardrop or loud laugh in so many unexpected places.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: CODA, much of it filmed on location in Gloucester, has sentiment without being saccharine or too cynical. Most of all, the story has heart.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: ...this is what great filmmaking is all about. It makes you feel something real. It's inspirational in a way few movies achieve.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: While it's predictable and a bit earthy for a PG-13 movie, "CODA" is a sweet-natured and touching drama with terrific performances.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: This coming-of-age story about a child of Deaf adults exploring her passion for singing will make you laugh, cry, and call your mom.
reviews.author: Emily Tannenbaum

reviews.text: As effective as it is -- and it is an effective tearjerker -- it does go down the checklist of things to push your buttons on. It's almost like a really well-designed Broadway show.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: You will cry in the best possible ways, even though you know better. It's kind of formulaic, but it's just so warm and true.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: This is a familiar kind of story, but it sidesteps the clichés and the formula to be something quite moving... This is a "feel good movie" in the best sense.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: It's a wonderful film, and the more people who watch it, the more likely the entertainment industry will be to cast deaf actors and feature deaf stories.
reviews.author: Erin Schoen Marsh

reviews.text: It's just about a family, and that's where the humanity is in this movie. It's heartwarming and sweet.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: As with so much in CODA, it's simple - but so beautifully executed.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: In the hands of any other filmmaker, this could have only been a movie about being taken for granted by your family. But in Helder's assured hands, CODA becomes a movie about being rescued -- by your family, and from your family. The nuance is admirable.
reviews.author: Poulomi Das

reviews.text: One of the most brilliant things about CODA is Heder cast actors who are actually deaf to play these family roles, layering in authenticity. It almost gives the movie a head start in believability.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: The conflict is unique, but the dynamic is universal...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Ruby is a gifted singer...a feel-good coming-of-age comedy...
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Yes, it's formulaic, with foreseeable TV-like beats, but there's a reason this winsome indie film broke all Sundance Festival sales records. The most feel-good Sundance hit since Little Miss Sunshine, it's an irresistible coming-of-age tale.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: The film is built on well-worn tropes and cliches, but manages to create something genuinely new and moving out of them.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Coda is a small movie, exquisitely made. Touching, funny and stirring, it would be the kind of movie you'd urge a friend to run out and see, except they'll only need to stay home and ante up to stream it on Apple TV+.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A heartfelt depiction of a family that will make you laugh, cry, and just leave you feeling all kinds of warm and fuzzy afterward. It's exactly the kind of movie we all probably need to see right now, earnest and hopeful down to the ground.
reviews.author: Lacy Baugher

reviews.text: Coda skillfully blends catchy musical numbers, a variety of nicely drawn characters, and a premise that brings the conflict between family obligation and individual dreams into poignant focus.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The knock here isn't that it's a blatantly feel-good movie... It's that it's like watching several of those kinds of movies jockeying for space, and the pile-up turning into something that's too much yet not enough.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: CODA isn't just authentic with its subjects in terms of their disability -- it's authentic with the treatment of their emotions, too.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: At first, CODA may seem like a simple little story about a high school girl coming into her own. She finds her voice and talents through music while struggling with pressures at home. It's a lesson in communication and the many forms it takes on.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: I'm going to warn you. This movie will absolutely wreck you in all the best ways. Never has "you'll laugh, you'll cry" rung so true.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: It's the film's considered, full-bodied engagement with Deaf culture that distinguishes and enlivens what is ultimately a very familiar, and aesthetically generic, story.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: I really enjoyed it for its sensitive portrayal of disability, for some genuine laughs, and for one scene near the end that I confess moved me to tears.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Winning Brit Emilia Jones helps light up feel-good film CODA. Eugenio Derbez is a wizard as the music teacher.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: There is a place for the crowd-pleaser, the tear-jerker, the movie that wants to manipulate your emotions and make you cry - particularly if it manages to bring something new to an old formula.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: If you're in the market for a heart-warmer, look no further.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Its brilliance lies in combining... well-tread tropes with an important sense of inclusion for a sweet story that truly sings.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: What "CODA" does so effectively is make this conflict a broader metaphor, for a teenager discovering the thing she loves and for her parents, even if they don't understand it, letting go and letting her pursue it.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Only an utter malcontent could prove entirely resistant to Coda's charms.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: At the heart of CODA is the gradual understanding that... you can love someone without being able to understand everything they love themselves.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Not only is it the best coming-of-age film since Bo Burnham's "Eighth Grade" (2018), but dare I say it's even better than Greta Gerwig's "Lady Bird" (2017). Until proven otherwise, it's the best movie of the year.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Caring, boisterous, and adorned with the hugest of hearts.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: CODA presents the traditional story of a young person finding herself couched in a non-traditional setting, and it makes the most of that combination.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: It's a powerful and engaging film in addition to being one that will thoroughly flush out your tear ducts.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: There's an authenticity and realness to these characters brought about by a combination of terrific acting and an outstanding script.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: The biggest heart of any film released in 2021 and the mix of outstanding performances for these multi-dimensional characters and an unexpected amount of humor raise the normally generic coming-of-age framing device into something special.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Jones is marvelous in a star-making role, lighting up the screen, her ASL an integral part of her performance, with a voice we know Berklee would be lucky to have on campus.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Easily one of my favorite films of the year. The pacing and the way director Sian Heder structures the story works really well in that it immediately immerses you in the characters' journey. Emilia Jones is quite a revelation.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Music is not only for the hearing, as we discover, and love is truly all you need.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Easily one of the best moviegoing experiences of 2021, CODA is an absolute joy.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Coda moves in a fairly predictable arc, but it does so sans apology and it does so well.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: [Jones] undeniably steals the show. But Matlin's performance poignantly captures what mothers everywhere go through when their children grow up and leave home to follow dreams of their own.
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: The story opens up/builds, expands and becomes grand opera-like in its emotional deliverance and character redemption. Plus it has one majestic final chord that keeps echoing.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Earnest and honest, CODA takes what could be a generic story and turns it into a heartfelt exploration of family and the benefits of inclusivity.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Writer/Director Sian Heder assembles an extraordinary cast of professional deaf actors along with hearing actress Emilia Jones in a stellar, layered performance. There is chemistry, pathos and humor throughout.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: A tearjerker, but one that's affecting rather than cloying.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Heder's delicate but realistic writing and compassionate directing avoids cliches.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: We might wish for a movie that centers a person who is deaf (baby steps, I guess) but "CODA's" depiction of Ruby as the outsider in her own family leads to plenty of rich, unexpected scenes.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: On balance, it's worth seeing despite its weakness for picking songs for Ruby to sing that reflect exactly what she's hiding inside.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Have some tissues handy.
reviews.author: Glenn Whipp

reviews.text: "CODA" is sweet, heartfelt, eye-opening and uplifting. It's a big hug of a movie, and we could all use a hug right now.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: strong performances make a standard story feel special
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Coda is all quirks on top and deeply conventional underneath.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Much of the credit deserves to go to writer-director Sian Heder (TV's Orange is the New Black), who has delivered a perfectly pitched balance of heart and humour.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: In pleading her case for the deaf, [Sian] Heder is mostly effective. You only wish she'd made a film as gritty as the people and places she's championing.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: [This is] exactly the kind of movie that will nail the sweet spot for many, many people.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: It's a beautiful story about the struggles with the family we are born into, learning to break out of one's shell, and finding music in the hearts of others.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The actors work together seamlessly, the blue-collar coastal setting is richly realized and the family's cohesiveness solidly established.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: CODA is a funny, easy-to-watch coming of age comedy that allows viewers to feel warm and understanding towards Deaf people. It's got Oscar nominations written all over it.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: There's a version of Siân Heder's film that might have been sincerely wonderful, and a real step forward for deaf representation. Alas, it's not this one at all.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Coda isn't merely a feel-good movie; it's the pinnacle of a new wave of post-Donald Trump cinema that can only be described as 'happycore'.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: "CODA" demonstrates that formulas are fine, if they're informed by true emotion and commitment.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: [T]he resulting drama becomes richer, deeper, and far more emotionally resonant than the story's foundation might suggest.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Coda killed earlier this year at Sundance, and now we know why: It's simply one of the best films of 2021, living up to all of the hype.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Writer/director Sian Heder weaves a beautiful, nuanced and complex tale buoyed by delicate and deft performances.
reviews.author: Amy Amatangelo

reviews.text: CODA is a wonderfully nuanced film, handling its subject matter with sensitivity, and carries within it a certain effervescence - a confident piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Heder's script finds excitingly fresh territory in the coming-of-age genre by bringing the audience into a complicated world that last year's "Sound of Metal" only hinted at.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: "CODA" is kindly and means well enough, boosted by select moments of real dramatic power that carry an otherwise fluffy effort.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Heder has finessed the story adroitly, putting a little more meat on the dramatic bones...
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: If it is not quite a masterpiece, it is only due to Heder's all encompassing ambition to produce a multi-faceted portrait of her heroine.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: What is surprising is the moving, even heartbreaking, way writer-director Heder tells Ruby's story without resorting to clichéd characterizations or syrupy sentimentality.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Coda is just a joy that I'm sure will be many people's favorite movie.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Pushes our buttons shamelessly, but also with enough sincerity, warmth and finesse to forestall accusations of rank manipulation.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The climactic emotional beats are telegraphed almost from the beginning, but they still hit hard, effectively leaving viewers who can suspend their disbelief feeling uplifted and dewy-eyed.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: What sets CODA apart from similar dramas is the central evolution not proving Ruby's alone. This is uncharted territory for them all.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The best crowd-pleaser since "In the Heights."
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Beyond its portrayal of a well-rounded deaf family, "CODA" may not revolutionary in its execution but it's like a memorable pop song: it has great hooks, a solid beat and it's fun to sing along to.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Two parts raw and real, one part manipulative, Coda finds engaging characters and real emotions in a hackneyed narrative arc.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Sometimes a feel-good story hits the spot. "CODA" is one of those times.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: ...a movie about joy and hardship, in which deafness is not a struggle but a way of life. Stepping out of the margins requires shining a light on the fullness of every community's humanity. That light shines here.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: The script is admittedly on-the-nose at times [...] but the emotions it elicits are strong and its praises are well earned.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: Writer-director Sian Heder's film is a genuinely sweet thing: The type of drama that loves its characters, and is determined to find a satisfying outcome for them.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Matlin, as always, is a joy to watch. But if there is a MVP in this Sundance Film Festival breakout hit and trophy winner, it clearly is the English-born Jones.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: CODA is confident and proud filmmaking that transcends familiarity by further layering the family dynamics here
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: CODA is a lucid, captivating and heartwarming coming-of-age film.
reviews.author: Aviva Dove-Viebahn

reviews.text: CODA intelligently and sensitively uses the [rom-com formula's] saccharine and familiar beats to its advantage.
reviews.author: Morris Yang

reviews.text: The best part about it is how it treats disability as something completely ordinary - analogous to first-generation immigrants not knowing English and depending on their bilingual children to translate.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Coda, even with all of its imperfections, drives home a truckload of emotions in its final act, filled with more silence than noise.
reviews.author: Michael Frank

reviews.text: A heartwarming coming of age story with an exceptional message of inclusion. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: CODA deserves to be the indie hit of 2021. You will laugh. You will definitely cry. I hope this beautiful film finds its audience when it hits Apple TV+ later this year.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Grounded and sweet, delicately bawdy, and decidedly hilarious, Coda puts an effervescent and original spin on the coming-of-age comedy-drama.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It's the kind of crowd-pleasing, heart-warming, kind of feel-good movie that can melt the most cynical of film critics' hearts.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: It's easy to forgive a few tired tropes when they're surrounded by such humanity.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Despite a plethora of coming-of-age story cliches, CODA still feels genuinely original, nuanced, and important because it has thoughtful, sensitive storytelling where it counts
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Much more than a manipulative story of familial tension.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: If you count Joni Mitchell's "Both Sides Now" as a favorite, get your tissues ready.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: By spotlighting the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing community, Sian Heder is finally bridging the gap and allowing the world to feel a little bigger.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: It's obvious, it's effective, and it goes down easy with dollops of feelgood positivity.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Sweet, thoughtful, and unusual in its extensive use of sign language and its casting of deaf actors (including Oscar winner Marlee Matlin), it's the kind of film you can't help but love.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's difficult to capture the beauty of Coda in words. It's something that needs to be experienced as a stepping stone for more deaf representation in film.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: With authentic performances, an incredibly solid script from top to bottom, and a respectful look into the deaf community, CODA hits all the right notes.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: When writer/director Siân Heder's script explores the daily challenges and accomplishments of a deaf family, it thrives. When it ventures into broad comedy, not so much.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Heder never makes any bones about this being the Universal Deaf Experience, but she approaches the tribulations of this specific deaf family with heart and authenticity.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: A charming heartwarmer that's good for the soul.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: The story beats of responsibilities vs dreams in the transition from teens to adulthood are pretty boilerplate. But Heder never overplays her hand with ill-judged sentimental excess.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Jones is stunning, gifted with a great singing voice, but also the ability to nail gritty authentic realism in a thinly sketched role
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The quartet of lead actors (Emilia Jones, Troy Kotsur, Marlee Matlin, and Daniel Durant) are all excellent, with Matlin especially poignant and hilarious and Durant showing leading man charisma.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: A witty, sweetly told drama about a hearing 17-year-old girl in a deaf Massachusetts fishing family.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: CODA is the kind of movie that makes you want to stand up and cheer.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: CODA is phenomenal. Writer/director Sian Heder is able to mix comedy and drama with aplomb, never once tripping over the cliches of the genre.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: But in the end, it's Jones' movie and the actor takes the opportunity and runs with it, serving notice that she's a multi-talented performer with a major career ahead of her.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The film is at its most moving in those rare moments when it's capturing the nourishing bonding ritual among a deaf family.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: In exchange for your suspension of disbelief, CODA gives you something warm and fuzzy, something that is nice enough as long as you keep your brain on sleep mode.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: It's likeable but very familiar.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: No surprises but strong hooks in Siân Heder's sweetly musical Sundance 2021 opener, which swept the main prizes in the fest's U.S. Dramatic Competition category.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: It's a wonderful thing to step into a world that may be unfamiliar to us, but ends up feeling like home.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: CODA cleverly remixes familiar coming-of-age tropes through its unique, insightful, affecting perspective.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: If CODA embraces overfamiliar story principles to normalize and universalize the experiences of the deaf community, it's at least wringing a noble purpose out of its conventionality. If you're going to do formula, do it that way.

reviews.text: [CODA] is a gentle film that looks at the core of a family (in this case a deaf family) and questions what it's like to need another person.

reviews.text: A traditional coming of age story with a twist about overcoming adversity while following a dream, with a touching performance by young Emilia Jones

reviews.text: The respect given to the deaf community told in the story is inspiring. It's heartwarming and funny, with a big level of sincerity shown by both Heder and her actors. A feel-good movie in the truest sense.
reviews.author: Reyzando Nawara

reviews.text: Coda, is a beautifully charming piece of cinema that highlights the differences that make us all unique, even if some may see them as shortcomings.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: A handful of sitcom-ish moments seem like small glitches in a script that works so winningly to bring the often unseen (or just terminally underexplored) world of deafness to such joyful, ordinary life.

reviews.text: CODA wears its coming-of-age tropes on its sleeve, but its confident construction and tender performances strike at the heart of what makes convention so effective.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: While CODA might seem undercooked, Heder pulls an emotional rawness out of the story.
reviews.author: Jas Keimig

reviews.text: CODA is the kind of movie that you can imagine getting a standing ovation at Sundance, if this were a year where people were allowed to gather in a stuffy Park City auditorium.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: A sweet, openhearted coming-of-age story that succeeds in spite of its own predictability.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: It's a crowd-pleaser, to be sure, and a little on the corny side, but it's so unwavering in its sincerity that it manages to hit all the right notes.

reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Even as we know where this story goes...we're fully on board for the journey with this charming cast for its sweet resolutions.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Though it hits the familiar notes of a teenage outcast yearning to break free and discover who she is, Heder's story delivers a refreshingly unique and, at times, tear-jerking look at growing up.
reviews.author: Rachel West

reviews.text: With a witty yet heartfelt script brilliantly brought to life by a fantastic cast, CODA is a real triumphant, bursting with emotion and charm.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Amid all the wise cracks and humour, there also remains the serious undercurrent of how people with disabilities are treated, and indeed how they should be treated.

reviews.text: CODA is beautiful, but it's just one story amongst so many others that have yet to be told, underlining an important message about inclusivity in films.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: The tearjerking moments arrive in waves in Coda's final act but, because they're come by so honestly, each swell and crest are welcome.

reviews.text: CODA is a charming and sensitive coming-of-age tale from director Sian Heder that also proves Emilia Jones is a star on the rise.

reviews.text: An undeniable charmer about juggling obligations to friends, family and self. When CODA hits the right notes in that balancing act, it's euphoric.

reviews.text: Too much of the film feels more informed by other movies than any real experience.

reviews.text: Sundance at its best - a breakout hit in the making.

reviews.text: My hope is that Coda will connect a lot of able-bodied people to many in the Deaf community who might feel like the world rejects and pities them.]

reviews.text: Authentic, sensitive, and playful, CODA remains human even as it tugs at the heartstrings.

reviews.text: It hits you right in the heart, not only as a moving story of what it means to be in a family, but also one about becoming your own person and following a dream.

reviews.text: Simultaneously classic and refreshing.

reviews.text: This is Jones' film and she gives one of those young performances that feel like a pronouncement of someone who will be around for years.

reviews.text: This was the beginning of one of the best opening nights I have had at Sundance in 19 years and this alone will make the evening of those who get to see it in the future.

reviews.text: A rare teen coming-of-age story that actually has something to say. Sundance 2021 was kicked off by this warm, hilarious, and must-see film.

reviews.text: CODA is a crowd-pleasing film that will bring about tears and laughter by the end...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Heder infuses such deep emotion in the movie, it makes up for its lack of narrative originality.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Good luck not shedding a tear not once, but two or three times in Coda's final act, as it's a feel-good tearjerker that pushes all the right buttons.

reviews.text: A heartwarming, powerful, and impactful film that will take viewers on quite a journey. The humor comes as a complete surprise and adds to the family dynamic.

reviews.text: Coda is a mostly likable concoction, but one that's just too formulaic and ultimately rather calculated to secure the emotional response it so desperately wants by the big finale.

reviews.text: A really special crowd-pleaser about unwavering support, unconditional love, and what it means to be a family. I'm still riding the wave of good vibes hours later.

reviews.text: CODA's one of those unassuming films, nothing particularly flashy about it, that takes you by surprise and makes you want to sing.

reviews.text: 19-year-old [Emilia]Jones is a revelation, carrying CODA on her shoulders, having learned American Sign Language for the part and finding every nuance in her performance, in both ASL and English.

reviews.text: Backed by a spectacular cast and Heder's emotionally charged script, Coda is an electrifying cinematic experience. Few films depict family drama so beautifully.

reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Heder works out all the family drama and fishing regulations with a light touch. All the characters have a sense of humor, all while really speaking their truths and emotions.

reviews.text: In its straightforward way, the film delivers an emotional knockout. It's a movie about a family, and by the end you may feel you know them as well as you know your own.

synopsis: Seventeen-year-old Ruby (Emilia Jones) is the sole hearing member of a deaf family -- a CODA, child of deaf adults. Her life revolves around acting as interpreter for her parents (Marlee Matlin, Troy Kotsur) and working on the family's struggling fishing boat every day before school with her father and older brother (Daniel Durant). But when Ruby joins her high school's choir club, she discovers a gift for singing and soon finds herself drawn to her duet partner Miles (Ferdia Walsh-Peelo). Encouraged by her enthusiastic, tough-love choirmaster (Eugenio Derbez) to apply to a prestigious music school, Ruby finds herself torn between the obligations she feels to her family and the pursuit of her own dreams.
